title: quant-degrade-eval-probes
content:
Purpose:
- Quick, messy notes to design a lightweight probe suite that detects accuracy/behaviour degradation after quantization+kernel changes on our serving runtime. Meant for local dev + nightly runs.

Background reading (short takeaways):
1) "Robust Quantization for Transformers" (ArXiv 2022) - summary:
   - Symmetric per-channel works best for attention weights; activations need bias-correction when using 8-bit.
   - Found large accuracy cliffs on rare tokens when range clipping is aggressive.
   - Takeaway: add token-frequency stratified probes.

2) "Layerwise Quant Eval" (ArXiv 2023) - summary:
   - Introduces per-layer sensitivity scores computed with Fisher information-ish approximations.
   - Good for prioritizing which layers to rollback or tune with fine-grained QAT.
   - Takeaway: compute sensitivity on small validation sets, cache scores.

3) Blog: "When 8-bit breaks (and how to find it)" - quick notes:
   - Real apps fail on rare long-context sequences and structured outputs (tables/json).
   - Tooling recommendation: compare distributions of logits and greedy-decoded outputs, not only perplexity.

Conference talk notes (MLSys 2026 session on quant/ops):
- Speaker A: emphasized streaming/kv-cache interactions with low-bit kernels -> small rounding changes accumulate across cache hits. Recommend: track drift metric on cached prefix tokens.
- Speaker B: deploy-time caching + async batching causes non-deterministic ordering; quantization amplifies diffs. Add deterministic seed checks in nightly.

Concrete probe ideas (to implement in eval harness):
- Mini prompt suites (fast, few-shot) that target known fragile behaviors:
  * rare-token probe: 40 prompts containing names/rare entities from token-frequency tail. Measure token-level top-1/5 shift.
  * structured-output probe: 30 table-to-json tasks; measure schema violation rate.
  * kv-cache drift probe: replay 100 real requests with long prefixes (1k tokens) and compare logits after 1,5,10 cache hits.
  * repetition/decoding probe: prompt that induces repetition; track PPL and % repeated tokens.

- Metrics to record:
  * delta_token_acc_top1 (vs baseline fp16)
  * KL_divergence_between_logits (avg across tokens)
  * schema_violation_rate (structured tasks)
  * latency p50/p95 (sanity)
  * cache_drift_index (fraction tokens with >X logits shift after cached prefix)

Quick implementation sketch:
- Harness: small python runner reusing existing evaluation infra in runtime/tests/eval_harness. New module quant_probes.py with a single-run JSON config for each probe.
- Baseline mode: run on fp16 wand use as reference. Compare deployments: fp16 vs int8 (symmetric/channels) vs int8-perf-optimized (our new kernels).
- Save outputs as compressed JSONL: {prompt_id, baseline_logits, test_logits, decoded_baseline, decoded_test, meta}. Only keep first 512 tokens to limit size.

Preliminary results (local, toy model Llama-7B-compat quant experiments):
- symmetric int8 w/out activation clipping: avg KL up 0.03, token top1 shift ~0.6%
- aggressive clipping at 6-sigma: KL up 0.18, token top1 shift 3.2%, structured output schema violations +9%
- kv-cache replay: small rounding causes drift after ~4 cache hits; drift_index ~0.12 (12% tokens exceed logistic shift threshold).
Notes: numbers noisy, need more runs + seeds.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Thresholds: what is acceptable delta? propose: token_top1 delta < 1% and schema_violation < 2% for a release candidate.  Need sign-off from product/solutions.
- Nightly vs pre-merge: some probes (kv-cache replay) expensive — run nightly; small fast probes (rare-token, structured) run on PRs.
- Rollback mechanism: integrate with rollout/A/B flags in console so can auto-fallback to fp16 or previous kernel if probe thresholds break.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Draft PR adding quant_probes harness (owner: Camila) — target: 2026-07-02
- [ ] Add rare-token probe set (owner: Sophia) — target: 2026-06-29
- [ ] Hook nightly job + SLO alerts for quant probe regressions (owner: Owen) — target: 2026-07-10
- [ ] Sync with product about acceptable thresholds (owner: Camila) — schedule meeting 2026-06-25

Notes-to-self / TODO when coding:
- Keep outputs deterministic: seed + sorted dicts + deterministic topk.
- Use mmap or streaming reader for logits to keep memory down.
- Add small utility to collapse logits differences into a single "drift score" for dashboards.
